documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66 y/o retired construction foreman transferring care; his prior internist is retiring. Brought every bottle plus his glargine pen.

Active issues he brings:
- Hypertension, years, on amlodipine 5 and metoprolol tartrate 50 BID. No home cuff.
- Type 2 diabetes on glargine 20 units at bedtime. Checks sugars a few mornings a week, mostly 130s-160s by his report. No lows he knows of.
- Atrial fibrillation, chronic, rate controlled on metoprolol, anticoagulated with warfarin 5 mg nightly for as long as he can remember, goal INR 2-3. Prior office did monthly finger sticks. No bleeding, no palpitations he notices.
- CKD stage 3 per his old office; he knows his kidneys are 'a little slow'.

PSH: gallbladder out around age 45. Left femur fracture at about 62, fixed with plate and screws.
FH: father had an MI at 72 and high blood pressure. Mother had diabetes and kidney disease. Brother had a stroke at 70.
SH: married, lives with wife in Granby. Smokes a pack a day, has for about 45 years. A drink or two on weekends. Denies other substances.
Allergies: none to medications.

ROS: no chest pressure, no dyspnea on stairs, no melena, no hematuria, no easy bruising, no foot numbness.

Exam: well appearing, weathered. BP and weight per flowsheet. Heart irregularly irregular, rate controlled, no murmur. Lungs with good air movement, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, old RUQ scar. Healed lateral left thigh scar. Feet: intact skin, monofilament normal both feet, pedal pulses present. No edema.

A/P:
1. Chronic AF on warfarin - we will take over INR monitoring, point-of-care INR today, then every 4 to 6 weeks with the nurse. Reviewed bleeding precautions and that new antibiotics or OTC pain relievers should go past us first.
2. HTN - at goal in the office today, continue current doses.
3. T2DM - A1c, urine albumin/creatinine today. Continue glargine 20 units.
4. CKD 3a - CMP today, avoid NSAIDs.
5. Tobacco - advised quitting in plain terms. He is not interested right now, 'smoked through worse'. Will keep asking. Qualifies for lung cancer screening: low-dose CT ordered after shared decision talk. AAA screening ultrasound ordered as well.
6. Health maintenance - records requested; PCV20 and high-dose flu given today. Hep C antibody once.

Return 3 months.

conditions.label: Risk of medication error due to look-alike drug confusion (LASA)

documents.title: Operative and anesthesia summary, hernia repair
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outpatient surgery summary - date of service 7/8/2025.
Patient: 68-year-old man. Procedure: repair of right inguinal hernia under general anesthesia. Allergies: NKDA.
Relevant history: hypertension, type 2 diabetes on insulin, chronic atrial fibrillation on warfarin (held 5 days per PCP plan; baseline INR 2.5 on 6/24), CKD stage 3.
Anesthesia: pre-induction BP 145/90. Surgical team asked for an IV antihypertensive bolus before induction. While drawing up, the anesthesiologist stopped on recognizing that the esmolol and ephedrine vials on the cart were near-identical in appearance and stored next to each other. Both vials checked against labels; correct agent confirmed before anything was drawn or given. No medication error reached the patient. Event filed with hospital safety reporting; patient flagged at risk for look-alike/sound-alike medication error for future anesthetics.
Operative course: uncomplicated repair. EBL minimal. Extubated in OR, uneventful recovery.
Disposition: discharged home same day with wife. Surgeon agrees with resuming warfarin this evening. Follow-up with surgery clinic as needed; PCP for INR.

documents.title: Post-op call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt day after hernia repair. Sore at incision, taking acetaminophen only - reminded no ibuprofen or naproxen with warfarin and his kidneys. Took his usual warfarin last night per surgeon. No bleeding through dressing, voiding fine, eating. He mentioned the anesthesia team told him they 'caught two look-alike bottles' before giving him anything; asked him to let us know if any summary comes home with him. INR set for 7/17.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check after surgery
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 1.7, expected 9 days after resuming from a 5-day hold. No bleeding, incision healing. Per PCP: continue 5 mg nightly, no extra dose, recheck in 12 days.

events.reason: sudden right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED provider note, date of service 1/6/2026, faxed copy.
CC: abrupt right-sided weakness, trouble talking.
HPI: 69M with HTN, T2DM on insulin, chronic AF on warfarin, CKD 3, hernia repair last summer. Per wife, fine before lying down for an afternoon nap; on waking could not get words out and his right arm and leg were weak. Brought by EMS.
Allergies: NKDA.
Vitals on arrival: BP 160/90, HR 78, irregularly irregular.
Exam: awake and alert, anxious. Expressive aphasia - comprehension preserved, halting nonfluent speech. Right arm and leg weakness.
Data: INR 3.8. Hgb 13.2. Creatinine 1.1. Urine drug screen positive for cocaine. Non-contrast CT head: left intracerebral hemorrhage.
ED course: stroke team at bedside. Warfarin reversed with 4-factor PCC and IV vitamin K. BP managed to target. Admitted to neuro ICU.
Impression: left intracerebral hemorrhage on warfarin with supratherapeutic INR.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Discharge summary (brief), admission 1/6/2026 - 1/12/2026.
Diagnoses: left intracerebral hemorrhage, warfarin-associated (INR 3.8, reversed in ED). Cocaine-induced cerebral vasculopathy.
Course: neuro ICU then stroke unit. CT angiography of the head: multifocal segmental narrowing of intracranial arteries; with positive cocaine screen, read as cocaine-related vasculopathy. Patient acknowledged intermittent cocaine use; counseled on abstinence. Aphasia and right-sided weakness improved through the stay; walking with supervision at discharge.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, insulin glargine 20 units qhs. WARFARIN STOPPED - do not restart until cleared by stroke neurology.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; stroke neurology clinic in about 6 weeks; outpatient PT and speech therapy referrals placed.

documents.title: Wife calling: patient in hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called to let us know he's been in the hospital since Tuesday with a bleed in the brain. Says he is talking better each day. ED note came by fax yesterday, given to PCP. Asked her to have the hospital fax the discharge summary and to book a visit within a week of discharge; scheduled for 1/16. Cancelled his standing INR appointment - warfarin is stopped.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with his wife, 4 days after discharge for a left intracerebral hemorrhage on warfarin (INR 3.8 in the ED). Discharge summary received 1/13: cocaine-related cerebral vasculopathy on CT angiography, cocaine screen positive.

He is embarrassed about the cocaine. Says it was 'here and there' with an old work friend, never daily, and that he has not used since and won't. Wife present and aware. Still smoking.

Speech: some pauses hunting for words, otherwise fluent, understands well. Right hand grip a bit weaker than left; walking on his own, slowly. PT and speech therapy start next week.

Meds reconciled: metoprolol tartrate 50 BID, amlodipine 5, glargine 20 units qhs. Warfarin stopped by the hospital; not restarting until stroke neurology weighs in (visit mid-February). He knows not to take any he has at home - wife bagged the bottle.

Exam: BP 134/82. HR irregular, rate controlled. Alert, mild word-finding pauses, follows complex commands. Right grip 4+/5, otherwise strength full. Gait slow, steady.

A/P:
1. Left ICH, anticoagulant-related, improving deficits. Therapy as arranged. BP at target, no change.
2. Cocaine-induced cerebral vasculopathy - abstinence discussed at length; resources given. He declines a referral for substance use counseling for now.
3. Chronic AF - off anticoagulation for now, rate controlled.
4. T2DM, CKD 3a - BMP, CBC today.
5. Tobacco - advised quitting, especially now.
Return after the neurology visit.

documents.body: This is his wife writing. Bob started speech therapy and physical therapy. They want to do 2 times a week each for 6 weeks. Is that okay with you, he gets tired. Also is it ok for him to drive yet.

documents.title: RE: Therapy question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi, thanks for the update. Yes, the therapy schedule is right on track and the tiredness is common after a brain bleed - rest between sessions is fine. Please hold off on driving until neurology clears him in February. Let us know if his speech or strength gets worse at any point - that would be a 911 call.

documents.body:
Saw stroke neurology on 2/17. No letter yet; per patient and wife, they told him he could go back on his blood thinner and could drive locally. Called neurology clinic during the visit (see phone note): confirmed clearance to resume warfarin.

Doing well. Speech pauses less often. Grip nearly back. Finishing PT next month. No cocaine since January. Still smoking.

Exam: BP per flowsheet. Irregular, rate controlled. Speech fluent with rare pause. Strength symmetric except trace right grip weakness.

Plan:
1. Chronic AF - restart warfarin 5 mg nightly; INR in 1 week, then weekly until stable. Reviewed bleeding warning signs again and the importance of steady dosing.
2. ICH recovery - continue therapy.
3. Cocaine abstinence - commended; continue.
4. Other chronic issues unchanged.

documents.title: Call to stroke neurology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with neurology clinic nurse about the 2/17 visit. Neurology attending's plan: OK to resume warfarin now, INR goal 2-3; repeat imaging only if new symptoms. Clinic letter to follow by fax.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check after restart
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 1.9 one week after restarting warfarin. No bleeding, no headache. Continue 5 mg nightly; recheck in 2 weeks.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range now. No bleeding. Same dose; next check 4 weeks. Neurology letter still not received - requested again.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months after the brain bleed. Finished PT and speech therapy. Strength back. Wife notices he still pauses for a word now and then, more when tired. Driving locally. No cocaine since January, which he volunteered. Still smoking.
On warfarin again since 2/19 without bleeding.
Exam: BP per flowsheet. Irregular, rate controlled. Speech fluent with an occasional pause. Strength 5/5 throughout, gait normal.
A/P: Bleeding complication closed out on the problem list; ICH and vasculopathy remain. AF - INR today, same dose. T2DM - A1c. CKD - BMP. CBC today, Hgb 12.5. Keep the September wellness visit.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR checked, reviewed. No bleeding, no falls. Continue 5 mg nightly. Next 5 weeks.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Need refills on the insulin pens and the metoprolol before the 4th of July please. Same pharmacy.

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sent both to your pharmacy, 90-day supply. Your INR check is due next week, please call to schedule.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Discharge summary, admitted 7/5/2026, discharged 7/12/2026.
Principal diagnosis: massive pulmonary embolism. Secondary: bleeding on IV heparin with hematuria and IV-site oozing.
Background: 69M, chronic AF on warfarin, prior warfarin-associated left ICH (1/2026) with cocaine-induced cerebral vasculopathy, HTN, T2DM, CKD 3. NKDA.
Course: admitted to ICU with massive PE on CT pulmonary angiogram; IV unfractionated heparin started. Hospital day 2 (7/6): new gross hematuria and persistent oozing from IV sites. BP 100/58, pulse 88, RR 18. Diffuse ecchymoses on both arms; abdomen mildly tender, not distended. Hgb 8.6 (baseline 12.5), platelets 220K, aPTT prolonged, PT normal. Heparin paused; resumed after 12 hours at a lower aPTT target once oozing stopped. No transfusion required. Hematuria cleared by day 5. Warfarin overlapped with heparin to therapeutic INR.
Note: admission PT normal despite warfarin on home list.
Discharge Hgb 9.4.
Discharge meds: warfarin 5 mg daily (INR goal 2-3), metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, insulin glargine 20 units qhs.
Follow-up: PCP in 2-3 days with CBC and INR; outpatient evaluation of hematuria.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two days home after a week-long admission for massive PE. Bled on heparin on day 2 - blood in the urine and oozing from IV sites, Hgb down to 8.6 - heparin paused and restarted lower, no transfusion. Discharged on warfarin 5 mg. Summary received yesterday; it notes his PT was normal on arrival.

Feels washed out. Short of breath on the stairs, better each day. No chest pain. Urine clear since the hospital. Bruises on the arms fading.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, saturating well on room air. Irregular, rate controlled. Lungs clear. Arms with fading yellow-green ecchymoses. Abdomen soft, nontender. Calves soft, no swelling.

Data: Hgb 10.1 today. INR 2.3.

A/P:
1. Massive PE, on warfarin - INR in range; weekly checks for now. Went over taking every dose; wife fills his pill box.
2. Bleeding on heparin, recovering - Hgb rising. Recheck in about 4 weeks.
3. Gross hematuria - cleared, but in a 69-year-old smoker it needs a urology evaluation regardless of the anticoagulation. Referral placed.
4. ICH history/cocaine vasculopathy - no new neuro symptoms.
5. Chronic issues unchanged; resume usual schedule.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR checked one week after discharge. No bleeding, urine clear, bruises nearly gone. Breathing better. Continue 5 mg nightly; next check 2 weeks.

documents.title: Urology appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Urology called. First opening is September 17. Is that soon enough or should I push.

documents.title: RE: Urology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: September 17 is fine since the bleeding has stopped. Take it. If you see blood in your urine again before then, call us that day.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One month after the PE admission. Energy mostly back, stairs fine. No bleeding, urine clear, no bruising. No cocaine. Still smoking.
Exam: irregular, rate controlled. Lungs clear. No ecchymoses. No leg swelling.
Data: Hgb 11.6, up from 10.1. INR 2.5. UA negative for blood.
A/P: Bleeding on heparin resolved - off the active list; gross hematuria stays open until urology. PE on warfarin, in range - INR every 2 weeks, then monthly. Anemia recovering. Hematuria resolved on UA; urology visit 9/17 stands. Annual wellness and diabetes labs at the September visit.
